text.p: Oil and gas producer Santos Ltd said on Wednesday it expected its operating profit after tax in 1997 to be comparable to the 1996 result.

"Operating profit after tax in 1997 is expected to be comparable to the 1996 result, subject to no material change in oil prices, exchange rates and interest rates," managing director Ross Adler said in a statement.
Santos earlier reported a net profit of A$195.9 million for calendar 1996, up 40 percent from A$139.9 million previously.
Adler said the strong result was due to record production and sales revenues, higher prices for all products and lower exploration write-downs.

The result was boosted by the A$200 million acquisition of the Australian assets of Parker and Parsley in 1996, and foreign exchange gains on U.S. dollar debt which offset the impact of a stronger Australian dollar, he said.
"After taking account of the adverse impact of the stronger Australian dollar on sales revenue but before gains on U.S. dollar debt, net profit after tax was A$179.9 million," Adler said.
This compared with A$150.1 million in 1995.
Adler said the company's large number of development projects and new contracts announced in 1996 set a firm foundation for production growth from 1998.
"The priorities in 1997 are to maintain our record of exploration success and to progress these projects on time and within budget," he said.
"At this stage of the year, it is expected that production volumes in 1997 will be similar to 1996 levels."

Santos is involved in the development of both the Stag oil field offshore Western Australia and the Elang/Kakatua oil fields offshore northern Australia, both of which are expected to begin production in 1998.
